name: equinox

attributes.attribute: fell midway in the Celtic seasonal cycle

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Celts marked the midpoints of the seasons, not the turning points. Their great festivals fell midway between the solar shifts. Winter began on Samhain, November 1. Spring began on Imbolc, February 1. Summer began on Beltane, May 1. Fall began on Lughnasa, August 1. These dates sit between the solstices of June and December and the equinoxes of March and September. Some scholars judge this calendar Irish rather than Celtic.

okr.objective: Rewrite the equinox entry to explain the Celtic seasonal midpoint calendar.
key_results: State that the Celts marked season midpoints, not turning points
Give the four festival dates of Samhain, Imbolc, Beltane, and Lughnasa
Place these dates between the solstices and equinoxes
Note the scholarly view that the calendar is Irish rather than Celtic
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2008, Introduction and s.v. Samhain, Imbolc, Beltane, Lughnasa.
